pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: Farmers markets are popular in the USA. Look at the cards and guess.

cards.note: Farmers sell their own fresh, seasonal food, often on weekends.
Many things are sold by the pound (lb): “Five dollars a pound.”
Some food is sold by the piece or in a bag or basket.

levels.A1: A pound is about half a kilo.
levels.B1: A pound (lb) is a unit of weight: about 0.45 kilos.
levels.B2: The US uses pounds, not kilos: one pound is roughly 454 grams, so two pounds is almost one kilo.

qs.q: What do you ask to know the price?
qs.pt: O que perguntar para saber o preço?

levels.B1: How much are the tomatoes a pound?

qs.q: How do you say the amount you want?
qs.pt: Como dizer a quantidade que você quer?

levels.A2: I’ll take a pound of strawberries.
levels.B1: I’ll take two pounds of tomatoes and a bag of apples.
levels.B2: Could I get a pound and a half of strawberries and a bag of those apples?

pages.compare: In Brazil we say “um quilo” and “uma dúzia”. In the USA people say “a pound” and “a dozen”. Which words do you use?

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: In -teen the stress is on the end: thir-TEEN. In -ty the stress is at the start: THIR-ty. Prices depend on it!

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: How much are the apples? I’ll take two pounds.
ladder.goal: Ask the price and say the amount.

ladder.say: Could you tell me how much a bag of lemons is? I need about ten.
Would you mind weighing these for me? I’d like roughly a pound and a half.
If you’re open to it, I’d be happy to take the whole basket for a better price.
Might we settle on a fair price, considering how generous the portion is?

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.
